signal.title: EAST: Embodied AI Safety Testing via Systematic Fault Injection in Digital Twins
signal.summary: 这项研究聚焦机器人操作任务，尝试把感知、语言理解和动作控制连接起来，完成更稳定的抓取或操作。

editorial.intro: 这项研究聚焦机器人操作任务，尝试把感知、语言理解和动作控制连接起来，完成更稳定的抓取或操作。
editorial.why_it_matters: 灵巧操作是具身智能最接近真实生产和服务场景的能力，也是检验模型泛化和控制可靠性的直接环节。
editorial.watch_next: 继续核对物体变化、未见场景和长序列操作中的成功率。

evidence.title: EAST: Embodied AI Safety Testing via Systematic Fault Injection in Digital Twins
evidence.excerpt: Task success is not a sufficient measure of safety for embodied artificial intelligence (AI), because robots may complete objectives while violating safety requirements. Existing evaluations often emphasize performance and robustness, but lack a systematic route from documented safety hazards to executable, verifiable tests. We present EAST (Embodied AI Safety Testing), a digital-twin framework that converts literature-grounded safety evidence into fault-injection tests across perception, instructions, environments, actions, and timing. EAST combines an expert-reviewed safety-fault taxonomy and eight executable operators with applicability and validity constraints. Its three-stage workflow generates test specifications, verifies fault realization during simulated execution, and independently assesses safety challenges, violations, task outcomes, and behavioral signatures using simulator-state evidence. The framework preserves execution traces and replayable records, supporting attribution and reproducibility across experiments. We evaluate EAST on six RoboTwin manipulation tasks and two policy architectures, ACT and RDT, against alternative testing strategies under matched budgets.
